key_insight: A learned patient world model can support multiple ICU policy simulations without rebuilding clinical states and transitions for each question.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can reuse a frozen patient-dynamics model while reconfiguring ICU resources, queues, and scenario-specific mappings to evaluate operational policies.
method: Train a neural patient world model on longitudinal MIMIC-IV EHRs.
Freeze the model and connect time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues.
Simulate bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity using scenario-specific mappings.
evidence_signal: The model matched Markov and semi-Markov comparators on aggregate occupancy and directional policy responses, reproduced policy gains from observed-trajectory replay, and captured a history-dependent 24-hour recovery contrast of −6.4 versus −6.7 observed percentage points.
watch_item: Performance beyond the studied ICU data and scenarios remains unestablished; deployment would require local validation of patient dynamics and scenario mappings.
paper_title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
